items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was he a Black man? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, Mel Williams.

ctx.x: He was a composer. He wrote some of the best music yet. He's the first Black man to walk in the control room and say, 'Wait a while. You all ain't doin' that right there. That's bad... How do you get more... Whyn't you raise up the body? Here, where do you get it to?' 'Well, we'll open this up.' 'Okay.' And he'd go out. Because I

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: So they tell, 'Well, Decca...Mel Williams is in town, and they're looking for talent, so why don't you go down there?' So I bring Lu down there, and she's singin' the Blues. So Mel Williams says, 'Ain't you got somethin' a little raunchy?'

ctx.x: Yes, Mel Williams. He was an All-American. Him and Fritz Pollard were on the same team, one of them teams that ran over everybody in the Eastern League...what do you call that league...? The Ivy League.
